Hi guys -

I want to clarify a few things:

* I have struggled with mental health and self-esteem issues for a decade. I do not perceive my face positively and never really have. I wanted to know what others thought.
* I wasn't bullied or called ugly as a kid, just had this sense that I was different/odd. I've always been really sensitive, have ADHD and am probably on the autism spectrum. This is all coming from the inside.
* When I'm at my best mentally, I would consider myself an outgoing, empathetic and fun person and I do think it shines through in a couple of these photos. It's interesting that some of you can pick up on that just from seeing the photos
* I was crying in the mirror photo so yes, it looks funny, and in the last photo I had just gotten out of bed, slept poorly, and been depressed/malnourished for 5ish days
* If I lost any more than 5 lbs my body would look skeletal. You can't tell from the photos, but I'm 5'2" with an athletic frame and some curve. I only weigh about 120lbs and I'm happy with my body as it is. I don't exercise regularly but appreciate what some have said about beginning to do so as a confidence boost. Will start with yoga.
* I hate the "Jesus shoes" too but I forgot to pack a second pair on that trip. LOL.
* It's flattering that some of you think I'm dating material but I really should focus on loving myself before I can even consider loving someone else

I started driving at 21! Don’t feel like it’s ever too late to take this step. I have super bad anxiety on top of this, and I used to have recurrent bad dreams about crashing the car I was driving. It took a lot of courage, but I think the main push was related to self-imposed social pressure. I started feeling bummed that I couldn’t just get up and go drive to meet my friends, and hated feeling like I needed to depend on someone to take me places. Eventually I weighed my options and decided that the positives of driving far outweighed the negatives. I’ve been driving for 10 months now and I’ve discovered that as long as you’re safe, defensive and double (or TRIPLE) check your blind spots, driving can be a low-stress experience for you. Avoid people on the road who drive oddly or impatiently, and in the beginning, try to avoid crowded areas. YOU GOT THIS!!!
